answer: New accounts start hollow, with zero trust weight, so spinning up fake peers costs real stake per identity and risks slashing across the linked cluster. Sybil resistance here relies on a staked beacon: each agent must lock verifiable collateral before voting, and every attestation emits a ripple through the reputation graph so colluding identities share linked history. Attackers thus face rising marginal cost per sybil while honest agents accumulate weight cheaply. This model fits agent Agent0280's threat model.
